text: Your Mercury years belong to learning, trade, and skill. That long chapter is not uniform, though, and the part of it running under the Sun puts a center in all the mental traffic. What you have been studying, writing, selling, or building starts to point somewhere, and that somewhere is usually you. This is often when a body of work gets your name on it. A course you finish, a piece you publish, a system you designed at work, a reputation for knowing one thing well: the stretch tends to attach your face to your competence. People come to you for the answer more often. Teaching, presenting, and speaking in front of a room fit this run, even if you would rather stay at your desk. The pairing also asks a harder question. Mercury will happily learn anything, while the Sun wants to know what any of it is for. Interests that were pure curiosity get sorted, and some of them quietly drop away because they were never really yours. Confidence in your own judgment usually rises, which is both the gift and the trap. Being right is pleasant enough to become a habit, and the version of it that stops listening costs you the very thing Mercury was handing you. Keep listening, and the run hands you a working voice with your signature on it, and the years after it have something solid to build on.

Under Venus, the mind turns toward what it likes. Your Mercury chapter is already about words, learning, and dealing; this part of it makes all three sociable. Conversations go easier. A negotiation that felt like arm-wrestling turns into a shared problem, and people who might have refused you say yes because they enjoy dealing with you. Work that mixes skill with beauty does especially well: design, music, editing for elegance, anything judged by taste as much as by function. Some people take up an art in this stretch. Others find the pleasure coming back to a craft that had hardened into a chore. Collaboration is the other theme. Co-writers, agents, partners, the person who does the half you are bad at, tend to show up in a run like this, and agreements made now often hold, because both sides actually wanted them. Study turns social too, since classrooms, workshops, and shared projects are where people meet each other. What can go quietly wrong is too much agreement. Words chosen to please can drift from words that are true, and a spell this pleasant can talk you into an arrangement you did not read closely. The awkward thing still needs saying, warmth or no warmth. With that much honesty in it, the run gives its best: work that is a pleasure to do, and people around you who make you better at it.

The first sub-period of any firdaria chapter goes to the chapter's own lord, which makes this stretch Mercury twice over: the theme of the whole thirteen years stated plainly, before any other planet colors it. Your mind wakes up. Curiosity returns with an appetite you may not have felt for years, and it arrives either as a specific hunger for one subject or as a general itch to know more of everything. Words multiply. You read more, talk more, write more, keep more notes, and the sheer volume of information moving through you goes up. Practical business picks up alongside it: paperwork, errands, arrangements, small negotiations, the moving parts of an ordinary life all wanting attention at once. Quick journeys suit the mood, and so does a schedule you keep rearranging. This is the run that sets the syllabus. What you begin studying here, in a school or on your own, often becomes the thread the rest of the chapter follows, which is worth knowing while there is still a choice about it. Nothing in this stretch slows you down, which is exactly the trouble: with no heavier planet steadying the pace, attention flies apart faster than usual. Ten open projects can feel like productivity until none of them close. Narrowed to a couple, with the rest left as reading, the doubled Mercury shows what it can do: the quickest and most flexible your thinking has been in a long time.

The Moon takes a stretch of your Mercury chapter and moves the thinking closer to home. The chapter's skill and study point themselves at family, memory, the household, and the ordinary business of a day. Talk with the people you live among matters more now than talk at work. Something may need saying to a parent, a sibling, or a partner, and this is a spell that supplies both the words and the willingness. Household arithmetic rises too: the move, the lease, the school, the budget, the hundred small decisions a home runs on. How you learn changes as well. You absorb rather than dissect, picking things up by repetition and by being near them, and formal study goes better when it attaches to something you already care about. Many people find they think best in company or in motion during this run, and worst alone at a desk late at night. Work aimed at a general audience suits the run, since the Moon's traditional business is with everyone rather than with specialists. Thinking can turn into circling, usually in the small hours, and circling is easy to mistake for analysis. Writing it down helps more than usual, because that gets the loop out of your head. At its best this run teaches your intelligence to serve your actual life instead of hovering above it.

School gets harder once Saturn has the running of part of the Mercury chapter, and that is not a complaint. The larger period is about skill; this is the portion where skill costs something. Study turns formal, or turns rigorous: an examination, a licence, an apprenticeship, a manuscript that wants three more drafts, a subject that will not give way to a quick pass. Progress feels slow because it is finally being measured properly. Your work tends to narrow here. You do fewer things and do them to a standard, and the projects that survive are the ones with real structure under them. Agreements made in this run bind in the ordinary sense, so reading the fine print becomes a skill rather than a chore. Concentration improves. A mind that ran on novelty learns to sit with one difficult thing, and that is the gain that lasts. The weight lands on your confidence. Saturn's self-criticism can go quiet and severe: you now know enough to see the flaws in your own work, and the temptation is to say nothing until it is perfect. Silence like that is expensive in a chapter built on exchange. Speaking while still imperfect is most of the discipline on offer. The end of it is fewer words carrying more freight, and a competence you no longer need to talk up, because it holds when someone tests it.

Jupiter's portion of the Mercury chapter widens the syllabus. Where Mercury collects, Jupiter asks what the collection is for, and this run tends to lift your learning out of the technical and toward the larger questions sitting under it. The scale of your audience often changes. Something you know gets taught, published, presented to more people than usual, or simply handed to someone who needed it, and the handing on counts as much as the knowing. Teaching in any form suits the stretch, including the informal kind where a younger colleague keeps coming to you with questions. Travel and study tend to braid together here. A course somewhere else, a trip that turns into an education, a language taken up because you suddenly have a reason for it: this run likes going to get what it wants to know. Institutions grow easier to deal with too, and a door your paperwork could not open may open on somebody's recommendation. Opinion can outrun the evidence in a stretch like this. It is easy to speak with more certainty than you have earned, to take on more subjects than a calendar allows, or to promise a piece of work at a size you cannot deliver. Enthusiasm signs things. With some skepticism left running underneath it, you finish the run knowing more than facts, which is the harder and better acquisition.

Mars sharpens whatever it is given, and given a share of Mercury's long chapter of study and exchange, it goes straight for the tongue. Argument comes easily in this stretch. You say the blunt thing sooner, cut through a stalled discussion, and lose patience with people who talk around a decision. That directness is an asset or a bill, depending on where you spend it. Work speeds up. Deadlines get met, backlogs clear, and a technical problem that needed stubborn attention finally gets it. Skills with an edge do well: anything mechanical, anything precise, anything competitive or done under pressure. Debate, bargaining, and open disagreement all suit the combination, and you tend to hold your ground better than usual. You may notice sharper company in your field, and their presence generally improves your work even when you dislike them. Speed is what costs you here. Words sent in heat are hard to call back, and a fast reply can cost far more than a slow one would have. Errors in this run come from speed rather than from ignorance, which makes rereading before you send worth more than any other correction you could make. Real courage is available too. The difficult conversation you have been rehearsing for a year is easier to start now. The heat does you good when it is pointed at the right target. You come out quicker, harder to push around, and less afraid of saying what you actually think.
